Date a restored page at the merge base in the page-metadata gate (#267)

The page-metadata gate now dates a page at the merge base of HEAD and
refs/remotes/origin/main only when there is exactly 1 merge base, the
page's mode and blob at HEAD equal its mode and blob at that base, and
git hash-object of the working-tree path gives its blob at HEAD. git
hash-object applies the attributes and filters that git reads and can
apply, such as those set in the repository, in the user's or the
system's attributes file, or in local, global, system or environment
configuration, follows a symbolic link and does not compare the
working-tree mode. An attribute or a filter that is not required and
that git cannot apply makes git hash-object hash the bytes as they are.
A branch whose own commits changed a page and then restored it exactly,
with main's stamp kept, is then not asked to restamp it. Otherwise the
gate reads the date at HEAD as before, and a committed date-only stamp
change or committed mode-only change counts as a change. A failed git
call stops the gate with exit 3, so it is not read as an absent blob or
a match, and so does git that cannot be run, such as when it is not on
PATH, and git output that the gate cannot use, such as a byte that is
not ASCII in a date. Output of a form that git does not print for a
reading stops the gate with exit 3, such as a shallow status other than
the 1 line true or false, a merge base line that is not 1 object name or
that repeats another line, object names of different lengths among those
read for a page, the names in the ref listing, which hold the protected
ref's tip, the merge bases, the names in the tree entries, whether blob,
tree or gitlink, and the git hash-object result, as git prints the
object names of a repository at 1 length, a ref listing line whose name
neither is the protected ref nor starts with it and a slash, a tree
entry that is not a mode and type pair that git prints and an object
name at the page's path, or a date line that is not 1 calendar date; the
name of a ref below the protected ref is not checked against the refname
rules of git. Before, a shallow status other than true read as full
history. The gate's docstring now lists each cause of exit 3.

The gate reads git's output as bytes, with no decoding or newline
translation. It splits the tree listing at each NUL byte, each entry at
its first tab and the part before that tab at each single space, and
compares the name after that tab, as bytes, with the page's path; it
splits the ref listing at each line feed and each line at its first
space, and compares the refname, as bytes, with the protected ref. So a
CR in a page's folder or a Unicode line separator in a ref's name is
read as it is. Dates, merge bases, object names and modes are decoded as
ASCII, and the readings other than these 2 listings split the output at
each line feed, with which it must end unless it is empty. git runs with
GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS set and without the other pathspec variables, so a
page path is read as that path and not as a glob; before, a page in a
folder such as [ab] was dated by the commits of a page that the glob
matched, such as site/a/index.html. The report prints each line with
print(), with each byte of a page path that the file system encoding
cannot decode shown as a backslash escape, such as \xff for 0xff, and
every other character as main's gate prints it, so such a page no longer
stops the gate with a traceback when stdout's error handler is strict.

The page-metadata suite gains a class whose cases each run in a
temporary git repository made with no template. Each folder that a test
of the class makes sits in 1 temporary folder that is removed when the
test ends. Each commit the class makes has a fixed date, and each check
of a page in it passes a fixed today, including the checks that the
gate's main() makes in it. Its git calls and the gate's read no system
or global configuration, no configuration from GIT_ variables, no user
attributes or ignore file and no system attributes file. Its cases plant
configuration from GIT_ variables, a ~/.gitconfig, a system
configuration file, and user attributes and ignore files at both default
paths. No case plants a system attributes file, since git has no
variable that moves it. No case checks dropping GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL alone
or HOME alone, since git reads a user's ~/.gitconfig only when both are
dropped, and the ~/.gitconfig case fails when both are. Cases pin the
date readings at merges: a branch restamp that main merges fails when
the last-change reading follows only first parents or uses
--full-history, a page added on a merged branch fails when the
added-date reading follows only first parents, and a page added
identically on both sides of a merge fails when that reading uses
--full-history. Cases pin pages in folders named [ab], by a CR, by a TAB
or by the byte 0xff, refs named across a Unicode line separator, the 4
pathspec variables, each set to 1 and to a value that git refuses, and
the report on a strict stdout, on io.StringIO, with no stdout and under
an ascii file system encoding. Cases give the gate, through a git on
PATH, output of a form that git does not print, and pin the escape of
each lone surrogate from \udc80 to \udcff in the report, the number of
git calls for a page, the fixed today that main() reads, a sibling tool
that is a symbolic link, a sitemap configuration that the engine
refuses, no content pages, git var naming no system attributes file, a
git on PATH that cannot be executed, a page added, removed and added
again, each required meta property missing, a ref listing line below the
protected ref whose name git does not print, a tree entry with an empty
name, a meta property with no content, an empty stamp, an empty meta
author, an empty or false co-author entry, an author with no entry, an
author name padded at its ends by each character for which str.isspace()
is true, such as U+0085, U+00A0, U+3000 and U+001C to U+001F, which the
gate removes, or by any other, such as U+200B or U+2060, which it keeps,
checked over every code point, a null author entry beside the meta
author, an ld+json type with ASCII white space at its ends or in
capitals, which is collected, or with other white space, U+200B or
U+2060 at its ends, which is not, an empty ld+json script left open at
the end of a page, another element's end tag in a self-closed ld+json
script, an @type list, an element other than a script with the ld+json
type, the trim of git's stderr in the message of a failed git call,
checked over every code point other than a surrogate, a page restored
exactly in a SHA-256 repository, an added date followed by a line that
is not a date, 2 pages that disagree on the author, a page with an
absent or empty meta author beside 2 pages that agree, the gate run as a
script, each primary JSON-LD type, each name that the gate needs from a
sibling tool, a sibling tool that cannot be read or that exits, JSON-LD
nested too deeply to parse, a page that is a folder, a JSON-LD member
that is not an object, and the date checks on a stamp that is absent,
malformed, of today or in Arabic-Indic digits, on a page with no history
and on a page in the published overrides. The class still takes inputs
from the machine, such as the git binary found on PATH and its built-in
defaults.

The suite drives the gate's ASCII, form and length checks from 1 table
of 24 readings, chosen by the distinctions that the gate's code makes: a
ref listing line, the protected ref's or one below it, at line 1, 2 or
3, including a line below the protected ref listed first, before the
protected ref's line, or second, after it; a merge base, at line 1 or 2;
a tree entry of each of the 5 mode and type pairs, at HEAD and at the
merge base; the git hash-object result; and the shallow status, the
added date and the last-change date. 1 case gives the 21 object names in
the table, in a SHA-1 and in a SHA-256 repository, the byte 0xff before
the name, a name of the repository's length whose last digit is /, :, a
backtick, g or A, and, where a length applies, a name of the other
object format's length; it gives the 3 other readings the byte 0xff. It
also gives each input that the per-site cases it replaces gave, in the
object format and with the message of its case, to each reading that its
case gave it, save a blob entry with 1 more digit, which answered every
git ls-tree call and now answers the first, so it drops none of those
inputs. It gives some to more readings than those cases did: they gave
39, 41, 63 and 65 digits on a first line below the protected ref and as
the git hash-object result, and 88 and 104 digits as the git hash-object
result alone, and it gives all 6 to each listing's first line alone,
where no length applies, and to the git hash-object result. It expects
exit 3 and the message of the fault's check for the row's git call. A
second case parses the gate and expects its 39 sites, each use or
definition of a name that reads or checks git's output, to match the
table's list of sites, each line that 2 searches for those names find
outside a docstring or a comment to hold a site, each check that a row
has to be applied at a site that the row reaches, and each check at a
site to be driven by a row of the table, save the mode decode in
blob_at(). So a site added to the gate, removed from it or moved to
another function fails the suite until the table names it, as does a row
that claims a check that is applied at none of the sites that the row
names or reaches. For each of the table's 64 cells, a reading and a
check that applies to it, a mutant of the gate that skips that check for
that reading's output alone fails the first case.

Residuals remain. History shapes that the cases do not build stay
unpinned, such as a branch that merged main after main changed the page,
a rebase, a squash merge of a branch with no net change, and a renamed
page, since the date reading does not follow renames. With more than 1
merge base, such as after a criss-cross merge, the gate reads at HEAD,
so a page restored exactly there is asked to restamp. A protected ref
that is absent, stale or not the remote's main changes the reading: in a
clone without that ref, such as a remote-less clone or a CI checkout
that does not create the ref, the gate reads at HEAD, as it does for a
ref that git for-each-ref does not list, such as a dangling symbolic
ref; in a clone of a fork, the base comes from the fork's main; and with
a stale ref, the base is older main. The working-tree check can differ
from what staging keeps: an exact restore of a page that is a symbolic
link, or of a page committed with CRLF line ends under core.autocrlf, is
asked to restamp; an uncommitted change can be exempt, such as an edit
that a clean filter set in the repository or in global, system or
environment configuration maps back to the committed blob, or an
uncommitted mode-only change; and a page can be exempt where staging it
would fail, such as under a working-tree-encoding attribute that git
cannot apply to its bytes. Ambient inputs that git reads can change or
redirect the gate's git calls, as on main, such as GIT_ variables other
than the pathspec variables, such as GIT_DIR, which redirects its reads;
git configuration, such as log.follow in the repository, global or XDG
configuration, which makes the added-date reading follow renames; and
replace refs, such as a replacement of main's tip, which the merge-base
reading and the readings at the base also consume. The future-stamp
check still reads today's date from the wall clock. When the exemption
does not apply, the reading at HEAD still ignores the working tree, so
an uncommitted edit of a page that is not an exact restore is dated by
its last commit, such as an edit made after the last commit of a branch
that changed the page. The report names a byte of a page path that the
file system encoding cannot decode with a backslash escape, so it reads
the same as a path that holds that escape's characters; under an ascii
file system encoding that includes each byte of a UTF-8 path, such as
\xc3\xa9, which main's gate writes as bytes to a stdout whose error
handler is surrogateescape. A stdout whose encoding cannot encode a
character of a line, such as an accented author name on an ASCII stdout
with a strict error handler, still raises, as on main. While file
descriptor 2 is open, an exit-3 message on stderr shows such a byte as a
backslash escape; with it closed, die() writes to stdout, as on main,
and raises on a stdout whose error handler is strict. Each page costs
from 1 to 5 more git calls, such as a ref lookup and a merge base
repeated per page. The object-name table's scope is its 24 readings and
the faults that it gives them: a weakening limited to an input that the
table does not vary, such as a listing's fourth line, can pass the
suite, and a replacing decode of the mode in blob_at() passes it, since
that mode is ASCII digits once TREE_ENTRIES admits it. The comparison of
the gate with the table reads call sites, not data flow, so a new
reading that uses none of the names it lists is not seen, and it takes
the sites that a row names as given, so a row that names a site that its
output does not pass through can claim a check that the gate does not
apply to that output.
